title: The Sicilian Table — Olive Oil and the Secret to Living Well
excerpt: Sicily has one of the highest concentrations of centenarians in Europe. The secret is not a supplement — it is a way of eating that begins and ends with olive oil.
body:
My nonna lived to ninety-four. She never set foot in a gym, never counted a calorie, never heard the word "superfood." What she did, every single day, was cook with olive oil — Sicilian olive oil, cold-pressed, green-gold, peppery enough to catch in your throat.

Science has caught up with what Sicilian grandmothers always knew. The PREDIMED study, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, followed over 7,400 people and found that those on a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil had a 30 percent lower risk of heart attack, stroke, and cardiovascular death compared to those on a low-fat diet. A separate study tracking more than 40,000 people over four years found that regular olive oil consumption was associated with significantly lower mortality rates.

But the Sicilian secret is not just olive oil. It is what olive oil makes possible: a way of cooking built on vegetables, legumes, fresh herbs, and time.

In a Sicilian kitchen, you do not rush. A proper caponata simmers for forty minutes. Pasta con le sarde needs patience for the fennel to soften. Even a simple insalata — tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion — gets dressed with oil and left to sit, so the flavors marry.

The polyphenols in extra-virgin olive oil are powerful anti-inflammatory compounds. Researchers at the University of Palermo found that these polyphenols, concentrated in Sicilian varieties like Nocellara del Belice and Cerasuola, can act as hormetins — mild stressors that activate the body's own defense and repair pathways. This is part of why populations in western Sicily have historically shown lower rates of chronic disease.

But there is a deeper lesson here. The Mediterranean diet works not just because of what you eat, but because of how you eat. Long meals. Conversation. Bread broken with family. Seasonal produce from the garden, not a package. The table is where health and happiness converge.

My advice is simple: buy the best olive oil you can afford. Use it generously. Cook slowly. Sit down to eat. This is not a diet — it is a life.
author: Milly Farfalla
